description: The mathematics of signals and the systems that transform them: continuous- and discrete-time signals, linear time-invariant systems and convolution, Fourier series and transforms, frequency response, sampling and aliasing, and the Laplace and z-transforms. Every transform is computed by hand and then explored interactively in the browser, where students sketch signals, convolve them and hear the effect of filtering and aliasing.
modelledOn: Oppenheim, Willsky and Nawab, Signals and Systems
Haykin and Van Veen, Signals and Systems
outcomes: Classify and manipulate continuous- and discrete-time signals and determine the properties of a system from its description.
Compute the response of linear time-invariant systems by convolution and by solving differential and difference equations.
Represent periodic and aperiodic signals with Fourier series and transforms and interpret frequency response in magnitude and phase.
Apply the sampling theorem to choose sampling rates, predict aliasing and design reconstruction.
Analyse causality, stability and transient response with the Laplace transform and the z-transform using poles, zeros and regions of convergence.

units.title: Continuous and discrete-time signals
topics: Continuous-time and discrete-time signals; analogue, sampled and digital signals
Transformations of the independent variable: shifting, scaling and reversal
Even and odd, periodic and aperiodic, energy and power signals
Elementary signals: unit step, unit impulse, ramp, real and complex exponentials, sinusoids
Periodicity of discrete-time sinusoids and the uniqueness of discrete frequencies
Real signals: an ECG trace, a voice recording and a day of national grid electricity demand

units.title: Systems and their properties
topics: Systems as mappings from input to output; block diagram notation
Memory, causality, invertibility and BIBO stability
Linearity and time invariance, with tests and counter-examples
Series, parallel and feedback interconnections
Systems described by linear constant-coefficient differential and difference equations

units.title: Linear time-invariant systems and convolution
topics: Impulse response and the representation of signals as sums of shifted impulses
The convolution sum and the convolution integral; graphical convolution step by step
Properties of convolution: commutative, associative and distributive; LTI systems in series and parallel
Causality, stability and memory read from the impulse response; step response
Solving differential and difference equations: natural and forced response, zero-state and zero-input response
Smoothing daily mobile money transaction counts with a moving-average system

units.title: Fourier series
topics: Complex exponentials as eigenfunctions of LTI systems
Continuous-time Fourier series: synthesis and analysis equations; trigonometric form
Convergence, Dirichlet conditions and the Gibbs phenomenon
Properties of Fourier series and Parseval's relation; line spectra
Discrete-time Fourier series
LTI response to periodic inputs; harmonics drawn from the mains by non-linear loads

units.title: Fourier transform and frequency response
topics: The continuous-time Fourier transform as the limit of the Fourier series; common transform pairs
Properties: linearity, shifting, scaling, duality, differentiation and Parseval's theorem
The convolution and multiplication properties; filtering as multiplication in frequency
The discrete-time Fourier transform and its periodicity
Frequency response: magnitude and phase, group delay, Bode plots; ideal and practical filters
Amplitude modulation and demodulation; how FM radio stations share the spectrum

units.title: Sampling and aliasing
topics: Impulse-train sampling and the Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem
Aliasing in time and frequency; anti-aliasing filters
Reconstruction: ideal band-limited interpolation, zero-order and first-order hold
Discrete-time processing of continuous-time signals
Quantisation in brief; why telephone speech is sampled at 8 kHz

units.title: The Laplace transform
topics: The bilateral Laplace transform and the region of convergence
Inverse Laplace transform by partial fractions
Properties of the Laplace transform; initial and final value theorems
System functions, poles and zeros; causality and stability in the s-plane
The unilateral transform for differential equations with initial conditions; circuit analysis in the s-domain
Block diagrams and feedback systems; a preview of control

units.title: The z-transform
topics: The z-transform and the region of convergence; common pairs
Inverse z-transform by partial fractions and power series
Properties of the z-transform; convolution becomes multiplication
System functions, poles and zeros, and stability relative to the unit circle
The unilateral z-transform for difference equations with initial conditions
Relating the z-transform, the DTFT and the Laplace transform; mapping the s-plane to the z-plane

units.title: Signals and systems in practice
topics: Removing 50 Hz mains hum from an ECG recording with a notch filter
Communication systems in outline: modulation, multiplexing and channel distortion
State-space descriptions in brief
Capstone: model, simulate and filter a real recorded signal end to end

schedule.title: Signals and their transformations
schedule.exercise: Sketch x(t) shifted, scaled and reversed for a given piecewise signal, writing the value at three points after each operation.

tasks.title: Plot a triangular pulse and its shifted, time-scaled and time-reversed versions on one set of axes, and read off five values
Split five signals into even and odd parts, classify each as energy or power, and compute the energy or average power numerically
Decide for ten given signals whether they are periodic, find the fundamental period of those that are, and verify by plotting

schedule.title: Elementary signals and real data
schedule.exercise: Show by hand why a discrete sinusoid is periodic only when its frequency is a rational multiple of 2 pi, with two examples.

tasks.title: Plot the unit step, ramp, decaying exponential and a sinusoid, and express a rectangular pulse using shifted unit steps
Plot discrete sinusoids at frequencies that differ by 2 pi and show they give identical sample values, explaining the uniqueness range
Load an ECG trace and a day of grid demand data, measure the dominant period of each, and describe the signal features you can identify

schedule.title: System properties
schedule.exercise: Test four given systems for linearity, time invariance, causality and memory, with a counter-example for each property that fails.

tasks.title: Classify five systems as having memory or not, causal or not, and stable or not, and check each with a bounded test input
Test a squaring system, a moving sum and a time-reversal system for linearity and time invariance with numerical counter-examples
Simulate a system described by a difference equation, test its BIBO stability for several coefficients, and relate the result to the interconnection of blocks

schedule.title: Convolution
schedule.exercise: Convolve two short sequences by hand with the flip-and-slide method and check the result against the tool.

tasks.title: Compute the convolution of two finite sequences of length four by the sum and verify the output length and the sum of values
Convolve a rectangular pulse with an exponential in continuous time, plot the stages of the overlap, and compare with the closed form
Verify the commutative, associative and distributive properties of convolution numerically, and find the single impulse response of a series-parallel interconnection

schedule.title: Impulse and step responses
schedule.exercise: Solve a first-order difference equation for its zero-input and zero-state responses and show that their sum equals the total response.

tasks.title: Find the impulse and step responses of a first-order system and decide causality and stability from the impulse response
Split the response of a second-order system into natural and forced parts, and into zero-input and zero-state parts, with plots
Smooth 90 days of daily mobile money transaction counts with moving averages of length 3, 7 and 14, and compare noise reduction against lag

schedule.title: Fourier series
schedule.exercise: Compute the Fourier series coefficients of a square wave by hand and sketch the first three partial sums.

tasks.title: Compute the Fourier series coefficients of a square wave and plot the sum of the first 1, 3 and 5 harmonics
Show the Gibbs phenomenon by adding up to 50 harmonics of a square wave, measure the overshoot, and check Parseval's relation
Pass a distorted mains waveform through an LTI filter and compute the power in each harmonic before and after, relating the result to non-linear loads

schedule.title: Continuous-time Fourier transform
schedule.exercise: Use transform pairs and properties to find the transform of a shifted, scaled rectangular pulse without integrating, and then check it.

tasks.title: Compute and plot the magnitude of the Fourier transform of a rectangular pulse and read off its first zero crossing
Verify the time-shift, scaling and duality properties of the Fourier transform numerically on a Gaussian pulse, with plots
Remove high-frequency noise from a signal by multiplying its spectrum with a low-pass mask, then compare the result with time-domain convolution

schedule.title: DTFT, frequency response and modulation
schedule.exercise: Sketch the magnitude response of an ideal low-pass filter and a practical filter, and list three ways the practical one departs from the ideal.

tasks.title: Plot the magnitude and phase response of a 5-point moving average filter and identify its null frequencies
Compute the DTFT of a short sequence over one period, show that it repeats every 2 pi, and find the response to a sinusoidal input
Amplitude-modulate a message onto a carrier, demodulate it with a low-pass filter, and measure the distortion when the filter cut-off is moved

schedule.title: Sampling
schedule.exercise: Explain why 8 kHz is enough for telephone speech, and what happens to a 5 kHz tone sampled at that rate.

tasks.title: Sample a 100 Hz sine at 1000 Hz and at 150 Hz, plot both and show which one aliases
Reconstruct a sampled signal with zero-order hold and ideal interpolation, and compare the errors for three sampling rates
Design an anti-aliasing filter and sampling rate for a 4 kHz band-limited signal, simulate the chain, and measure the aliasing error

schedule.title: The Laplace transform
schedule.exercise: Find the inverse Laplace transform of a rational function by partial fractions on paper, then confirm by simulation.

tasks.title: Find a partial fraction expansion of a rational Laplace transform with distinct poles and the corresponding time function
Use the initial and final value theorems on three transforms and check each result against the time response
Find the region of convergence for a two-sided exponential and show how different regions give causal, anti-causal and two-sided signals

schedule.title: System functions and circuits
schedule.exercise: Solve an RLC circuit with initial conditions in the s-domain and compare it with the time-domain solution.

tasks.title: Plot the poles and zeros of a system function and decide stability and causality from the region of convergence
Use the unilateral Laplace transform to solve a second-order differential equation with initial conditions, and plot the response
Close a feedback loop around a plant, find the poles as the gain changes, and identify the gain at which the system becomes unstable

schedule.title: The z-transform
schedule.exercise: Find the inverse z-transform of a rational function by partial fractions and by long division, and show that both agree.

tasks.title: Compute the z-transform of a few simple sequences and state the region of convergence of each
Invert a rational z-transform by partial fractions and by power series, and verify the first eight samples against the first method
Use the convolution property to find the output of a difference-equation system for a given input and check it against direct simulation

schedule.title: Applications and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone report: describe the signal, the model, the filter design and the results, with the before and after spectra of the recorded signal.

tasks.title: Place the poles and zeros of a discrete system on the z-plane and decide whether it is stable from the unit circle
Design a notch filter at 50 Hz, apply it to a noisy ECG recording, and compare the spectra before and after
Map s-plane poles to the z-plane with a sampling period of 1 ms and compare the analogue and discrete responses of a second-order system
Model, simulate and filter a recorded signal end to end, choosing sampling rate and filter, and report the measured improvement in signal-to-noise ratio
